exposure: residence in urban slums vs. rural areas
outcome: antenatal care (minimum three visits, antenatal card availability, Tetanus Toxoid immunization, Iron Folic Acid consumption)
intrapartum care (institutional delivery, accompanying of pregnant mothers for deliveries to institute by peripheral workers)
postnatal care (postnatal check-ups, family planning advice)
newborn care (newborn check-ups, early breastfeeding initiation, birth registration, prelacteal feed)
cohort: 216 rural and 377 urban slum mothers who delivered in the last year in the Tapi district and Surat Municipal Corporation in India
finding: Coverage and utilization of most maternal and newborn care services were higher in rural areas compared to urban slums, except for institutional delivery rate, use of family planning methods, and prelacteal feed, which were higher in urban slums.
